title: maxOdds acceptance probe — live, qa.liqd.com, 2026-09-01
evidentiaryStatus: AUDITOR-ATTESTED SESSION RECORD. This file is a structured transcription of the auditor's session notes for a live probe. Raw HTTP request/response pairs were NOT retained. Reformatting the note as JSON does not upgrade its evidentiary status: it is testimony, not a machine-checkable artifact, and no verification step reads it. It was previously carried as evidence/E14-maxodds-live-probe.md; the content is preserved verbatim in meaning, and this is the only copy.
purpose: Establish that a 9900x bet is ACCEPTED and SETTLED for `originals-dice`, i.e. that the operator's own config field `maxOdds 99` is not the settlement ceiling — after the config field and the game UI were found to disagree. Read-only inspection plus one live bet.
scopeWarning: This probes ACCEPTANCE AT 9900x. It does NOT establish (a) server REJECTION above 9900x — the above-9900x clamp observed was client-side in the UI; (b) a WINNING credit at 9900x — the probe bet lost; (c) the existence or shape of a maximum-exposure cap.

configField.note: Only one dice row exists. The `fast-games-17 maxOdds 10000` row seen at recon (2026-08-27) is no longer present.

ui.observation: Entering a multiplier above 9900 clamps to exactly 9900.00x at win chance 0.01%; 'Payout On Win' tracks stake x 9900. Entering 9999999 clamped straight back to 9900.00x.
ui.conclusion: The UI offers up to 9900x — 100x the config field's 99.
ui.limit: The clamp is CLIENT-SIDE. It says nothing about what the server would do with a higher multiplier.

liveBet.description: The decisive test — one real bet, $0.10, at multiplier 9900x.
liveBet.outcome: loss — as a 0.01% win-chance bet does 9,999 times in 10,000; the $0.10 stake was lost
liveBet.uiPayoutOnWin: 990.00000000 = 0.10 x 9900 — this is what the CLIENT displayed before the bet. The backend's WINNING payout at 9900x was not observed, because the probe bet lost.
liveBet.conclusion: The settlement backend accepts and settles 9900x, so the config field's 99 is not the real ceiling. This is not a UI-only display bug — the backend priced and settled 9900x.
liveBet.notRetained: the raw place-bet response (bet id, server seed id, nonce) and a subsequent rotated-seed reveal. Named as recapture item A1/10.

notAnExploit.argument: At 9900x the winning band is a single grid point. Under the verified half-open rule (roll < upper, band-width-independent — see E13 and finding F6) `under 0.01` wins only on roll 0.00 = 1/10,000 = exactly 99% RTP. No player-favourable bet.
notAnExploit.counterfactual: Inclusive-both-ends would have won on 2/10,000 = 198% RTP. That rule was retracted, which is why the boundary correction was load-bearing.
notAnExploit.reproducibleArithmetic: Independent of the live settlement, the ARITHMETIC of the 9900x extreme is pinned as unit vectors in tests/dice/rngTests.ts: quotedMultiplier of a width-0.01 band ([0, 0.01)) is exactly 9900x, discreteWinCount of that band is exactly 1 grid point, and its effectiveEdge is exactly 1.00% (99% RTP). The 'single grid point -> 99% RTP, not 198%' argument is therefore reproducible from the committed code without a settled bet at the extreme.

notVerified.item: The boundary at the 0.01 extreme was not witnessed in settlement.
notVerified.detail: A settled win at exactly roll 0.00 — or the decisive roll 0.01, which must LOSE — on an `under 0.01` band is a 1/10,000 event. The fairness of the extreme rests on the half-open proof (E13, at a mid-range boundary) plus the band-independent comparator, not on a settled bet at the extreme.
notVerified.remedy: targeted probe in the production-parity recapture

notVerified.item: The max-payout / exposure cap is uncharacterised.
notVerified.detail: 9,898 max bet x 9900x is about $98M theoretical; `maxExposureUsdc` was null in the config row. Whether a cap exists at all, and whether it would clip the payout or reject the bet, was NOT tested. This matters for RTP, not just operations: a cap that clips rather than rejects would reduce the realised RTP at capped stakes below the 99% this report verifies at the stakes actually captured.
notVerified.remedy: characterise the cap in the recapture

notVerified.item: The verify-endpoint confirmation at the extreme was not completed.
notVerified.detail: The session was rate-limited (an earlier scan tripped the limiter). The boundary rule is nonetheless established by E13 plus the comparator.

declaredLimitation: L7 — the 9900x ceiling and the input contract rest on this single live probe. Registered as an executed mutation survivor in tests/mutation-survivors.json ('published maxOdds ceiling raised far above the captured tail'): because no captured bet exceeds 99x, raising MAX_ODDS above the captured tail is invisible to every scored step. Shrinking it below the captured span IS caught (tests/mutations.json, 'published maxOdds ceiling shrunk below the captured tail', Step 10).
relatedFinding: F-LIMITS — a disclosure finding, not an exploit: the operator's config API misstates enforced behaviour, which is itself a trust-surface fact.
renameReason: Renamed 2026-09-11. This record is a session narrative — a config pull, a UI observation and one live bet — not a machine-checkable probe record. Under the previous name it matched the framework contract for evidence/*probe*.json (gate-premises P3), which requires a probes[] array with params and outcome per entry, and it has none. The honest fix is for the filename to stop claiming to be a probe record. The alternative — restructuring testimony into a probes[] array so the parser accepts it — would dress a session note as machine-checked evidence, which is exactly what this record's own evidentiaryStatus warns against.
